headlines: Bullish (NYSE:BLSH) Q3 2026 Results: EPS Beat and $300M Buyback Spark Relief Rally — ChartMill, 2026-11-18
Bullish 6-K: Q3 net income $576.3M, diluted EPS $3.57, adjusted revenue $84.4M from $76.5M — Moomoo, 2026-11-18
Bullish's Equiniti deal could remake it into a tokenization powerhouse, analysts say — CoinDesk
gappers.catalyst_detail: Q3 2026 landed pre-open (6-K) with the call at 08:30 ET. Adjusted revenue $84.4M vs $82.7M consensus (+2.0%) and non-GAAP EPS $0.12 vs $0.0894 (+34%); adjusted EBITDA $35.6M vs $28.6M a year ago at a 42% margin; adjusted net income $18.7M vs $13.8M; adjusted transaction revenue $28.0M vs $26.7M. Digital-asset sales FELL to $32.1B from $41.6B. The board authorized up to $300M of repurchases against a ~$2.9B cap (~10%), explicitly non-obligating and suspendable. The headline net income ($576.3M total / $555.9M attributable to owners, diluted EPS $3.57 vs $0.10) is NOT operating earnings: it is driven by a $598.4M fair-value gain on digital assets held. FY26 guidance covers subscription/services/other revenue $225-235M, adj opex $220-225M, finance expense $60-65M. Equiniti ($4.2B: $1.85B assumed debt + ~$2.35B stock) still guided to close January 2027. New this run: former NYSE Group President Stacey Cunningham has joined as President, and the Issuer Token Coalition now counts NYSE, SoFi and DriveWealth among members.
gappers.why: Revenue and EBITDA grew while platform volumes shrank — take-rate expansion, not demand growth. The operative lever is the buyback: ~10% of market cap authorized on a stock down 32.9% in a month and 13.2% in a week puts a standing bid under a de-rated float. This is a relief rally off a washed-out base, not a growth re-rating. Two numbers that circulated as bearish are basis errors, checked and dismissed: (a) a '35% guidance miss vs $368.0M consensus' compares a subscription-only guide to a total-revenue estimate — ChartMill independently flags the same non-comparability; (b) a Barchart snippet quoting 'Q3 revenue $35.9M vs $37.3M consensus' near BLSH belongs to a different company in a multi-stock article, contradicted by the 6-K's $84.4M.
gappers.impact: Sustainable-ish on company specifics, but the tape is the problem. Durable: a dated share-count reduction, Equiniti, and a credible market-infrastructure hire. The call was the key unknown and it passed — price went 20.50 -> 21.00 (high 21.38) across the 08:30 window on 15,293 shares, so the move survived management Q&A rather than fading. Premarket volume is now 79,362 and CLEARS the >=50k gate (it was 49,695 at 07:54 ET), though the 19.40-21.75 overnight range means the quoted gap is still fragile. Prior session 2.49M = 1.64x the 1.51M 20-day average: real participation, not a blow-off. Structure remains broken: -21.1% vs 20-SMA, -36.6% vs 50-SMA, -38.9% vs 200-SMA, RSI14 29.8. Sector read-through is the live risk — the driver is crypto beta and bitcoin is down ~1.1% today near $64,100 after six consecutive down weeks, so the parent tape still falls while this gaps up on company news.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The buyback, Equiniti and the Cunningham hire are structural, but this is a bounce off a 20-day low sitting below all three major SMAs with crypto beta still declining; the structural items are 2027 events, not this week's. The Financials-vs-crypto classification ambiguity tilted slightly toward market-infrastructure/Financials (a late-cycle favored sector) on the NYSE-pedigree hire and the NYSE/SoFi/DriveWealth coalition, but it still TRADES as crypto beta.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Zero open positions and $100,000 equity, so nothing would be displaced — the cost is one of three weekly trade slots and the attention of today's final 11:00 ET scan. It is the only one of the two that clears the mechanical gates: ATR14 $1.9335 (9.2% of price), so a 10% stop at $18.90 is 1.09 ATR (just outside an average day, survivable), and a +20% target at $25.20 sits inside the 20-day high of $29.87, so 2:1 R:R is reachable at a permitted stop distance. ATR sizing gives 517 sh (1.0% of equity per 1-ATR move) = ~$10,857, 10.9% of equity, inside the 20% cap. It now also clears the >=50k premarket gate it failed at 07:54. It fails on the rulebook, not the arithmetic: the 200-SMA long-bias filter ('only long when price > 200-SMA on daily') HARD-FAILS at -38.9%, which is exactly the bottom-fishing the strategy forbids, and confluence musters only 1 of 4 ({VWAP, RSI, 200-SMA, insider}) since RSI 29.8 is an oversold-bounce read rather than trend confirmation. Research only, no order.

gappers.catalyst: No company release today; the live catalyst is an analyst/model fair-value lift on the Nov 10 EDODM1 Phase 2 data (Simply Wall St fair value $10.19 -> $12.13), layered on a dilution-flush bounce after the Nov 11 $125M raise priced at $5.00.
headlines: PepGen (PEPG) Stock Sees Fair Value Lift After Encouraging EDODM1 Analyst Response — Small Caps Daily after-hours scan, 2026-11-18
PepGen (Nasdaq:PEPG) analyst price target moved higher, fair value rising from $10.19 to $12.13 as analysts respond to positive EDODM1 data — Simply Wall St
PEPG: 8 analysts, consensus Strong Buy, 12-month target $13.75 — StockAnalysis.com
gappers.catalyst_detail: No PepGen press release is dated Nov 17 or 18 — a correction to this run's own framing is that there IS nonetheless a documented catalyst, which the 07:09 and 08:09 runs recorded as 'no news': analyst and model fair-value revisions responding to the EDODM1 (DM1) data, with Simply Wall St's fair value lifted from $10.19 to $12.13 and consensus standing at Strong Buy across 8 analysts with a $13.75 12-month target. This is a second-order response to already-public data, not new clinical information. The underlying sequence: Nov 10 Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 10 mg/kg showed 46.5% mean splicing correction at Week 13 vs 6.8% placebo and vHOT improving 3.9s (~52.7%) vs 0.2s, with no serious AEs or discontinuations — the stock roughly doubled. Management monetized it the next afternoon: $125M priced Nov 11 at $5.00 for 25,000,000 shares, closed Nov 13, with a live 30-day option on 3.75M more. Q3 net loss $19.391M; cash $104.8M at Sept 30; runway into 2028 post-raise. Two standing overhangs: a US partial clinical hold REMAINS in force, with the planned 2H-2027 end-of-Phase-2 meeting contingent on its removal, and the next readout is January 2027 (OLE interim 5 mg/kg plus 10 mg/kg safety), with 12.5 mg/kg in H1 2027.
gappers.why: Offering overhang meeting a fresh analyst bid. Placing 25M shares at $5.00 handed the market a reference price; the stock broke under it and slid to $3.88 by Nov 17, ~22% below the deal. Today's +7% is a dilution-flush snapback — traders treating sub-$4 as a discount to what institutions just paid — now given a narrative assist by upward fair-value revisions on the Phase 2 data. No new company information, and the 3.75M-share underwriter option stays live as fresh supply.
gappers.impact: Reads as a bounce likely to mean-revert. Volume says participation is COOLING, not churning: prior session 5.62M = 0.69x the 8.17M consolidated 20-day average, consistent with post-deal rotation clearing rather than fresh demand. Premarket is thin at 45,309 shares in a tight 4.10-4.21 band, and it FAILS the >=50k gate — though it has closed most of the gap from 32,487 at 07:54, so a late-premarket clear is plausible and would be worth re-checking at 11:00 ET. The chart is an unresolved spike: 20-day range $2.22-$6.45 on a $4.16 price. Decisively for a swing, the nearest hard catalyst is January 2027 — weeks out — and the standing US partial clinical hold is an unresolved regulatory gate. Sector read-through nil: single-asset DM1 risk, no complex moving with it.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The Phase 2 data is structural but already priced and then diluted, and today's driver is an analyst revision to week-old information rather than new evidence; the next readout is January 2027 at the earliest and a partial clinical hold still gates the regulatory path. Speculative clinical-stage biotech is absent from the late-cycle favored set (Energy, Materials, Financials).
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace at zero open positions, so the cost is one of three weekly slots. PEPG is the only one of the two that PASSES the 200-SMA long-bias filter (+32.8%), and it is above its 20- and 50-SMA too — the cleaner trend by far. It fails on R:R, badly. ATR14 is $0.5425 = 13.0% of price, so a 10% stop at $3.744 is just 0.77 ATR — inside a single average day, so ordinary noise would take it out before the thesis resolved. Worse, the +20% target lands on $4.99, i.e. effectively the $5.00 offering price where 25M shares were placed: the target sits on the heaviest overhead supply in the book. Clearing 2:1 from a stop outside 1 ATR needs roughly a 14% stop and 28% target, and 14% breaches the 7-10% stop band. Confluence also fails at 1 of 4: the 200-SMA passes, RSI 58.5 is neutral, no insider signal is documented, and the catalyst is an analyst revision rather than a company event. The two names remain mirror images — BLSH clears R:R and hard-fails the 200-SMA, PEPG clears the 200-SMA and fails R:R — and neither is takeable. ATR sizing would be 1,843 sh = ~$7,667, 7.7% of equity. Research only, no order.
